A1.justification: Both PDFs describe UGPhysics and its MARJ evaluation pipeline. All 29 pages of each version, including Appendices A–D, are readable and support comparison; corresponding content can be matched across relocation and table renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of 31 LLMs, MARJ agreement with human judgments on 100 examples, error analysis, and data-leakage measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains these empirical results and adds evaluations of two models, comparisons with other benchmarks, and token-consumption and generation-budget experiments.

M1.justification: The two-stage MARJ procedure, answer-type handling, rule-based matching, and GPT-4o fallback remain unchanged. Section 3.3, Appendix B.4, and Algorithm 1 describe the same method.

E1.justification: Section 5.5 adds reported GPT-4o evaluations on MMLU college, high-school, and conceptual physics, MMLU-pro, OlympicArena, GPQA, and MATH, plus a MATH token-use comparison. This substantially broadens evaluated coverage beyond UGPhysics to additional educational levels and mathematical reasoning. UGPhysics itself retains the same problems, subjects, and languages.

E2.justification: Table 5 adds Phi-4 and full DeepSeek-R1 while retaining all 31 previously evaluated models. Full DeepSeek-R1 is distinct from the distilled variants already evaluated in v1; this is a limited expansion of the comparison set.

E3.justification: The original prompts, decoding settings, and Appendix B.3 budgets remain unchanged. v3 adds token-use and clipping metrics, uncapped DeepSeek-R1 API evaluation, and an additional generation-budget condition: 16,384 tokens in the prose, labeled 16,382 in Tables 8–9, compared with the existing 8,192-token condition.

E4.justification: Sections 5.5–5.6 add computational-cost analysis and a systematic test of whether generation limits explain poor performance. Tables 8–9 examine clipping and accuracy across two budgets for five reasoning models. These introduce substantial new sensitivity evidence beyond the retained subject, language, human-validation, leakage, and error analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests, and v3 introduces no uncertainty-estimation procedure. The added accuracy and clipping percentages are additional results, not a change in uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v3 adds model, benchmark, token-use, and budget-dependent results while retaining all original Table 5 rows and appendix scores. For example, Table 9 reports DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-70B at 40.17% versus 41.77% under different budgets. The new Phi-4 and DeepSeek-R1 averages are printed as 0.3530 and 0.5634 despite the percentage caption, leaving their scale ambiguous. Section 5.1 also changes 27.0/22.9/13.8% to 31.0/26.7/16.5%, matching the retained Figure 2.

T1.justification: There are no added or revised theorems, proofs, formal assumptions, or mathematical derivations. MARJ's mathematical matching rules and the worked physics examples remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory findings, and conclusion retain the same benchmark and MARJ contributions and claims about physics reasoning. They also retain the 31-model evaluation and o1-mini's highest accuracy of 49.8%; the added model results are not incorporated into revised headline claims.

C2.justification: Section 5.5 newly interprets cross-benchmark accuracy and token consumption as evidence of UGPhysics's difficulty and computational demands. Section 5.6 interprets modest gains from longer generations as motivation to address token redundancy. Existing explanations of subject, skill, language, and error patterns, and the stated future extensions, remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 3.2 now identifies the source as seven books from The Great Compendium of Physics Problems, rather than unspecified exercise books. The abstract adds a code/data availability statement and repository address. Existing appendix implementation details and prompts are retained; the PDFs alone do not verify repository contents.

R1.justification: v3 adds references to Didolkar et al. on metacognitive evaluation and Chen et al. on overthinking, and includes TheoremQA in the descriptive benchmark comparison in Table 1. These are targeted additions; the broader research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 adds Sections 5.5–5.6 and acknowledgments, renames Section 3.1, updates publication and affiliation text, and makes localized explanatory edits. Most existing prose, the overall section sequence, and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains a row, Table 5 gains a new-results block, and Tables 7–9 are added. Existing tables and figures shift within the main text, while appendix tables are renumbered without substantive display changes. The figures themselves remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 adds useful token-budget checks, benchmark context, source details, and access information, and aligns Section 5.1 with Figure 2. However, its new Table 5 rows have ambiguous units while the headline model count and best-model claims remain unreconciled. Section 5.6 also describes residual clipping as small despite Table 8 reporting 34.47–43.80% for several models. The added evidence improves transparency, but these new inconsistencies impair interpretation enough that a reliable net quality judgment is unclear.
